texts: Supravalvar aortic stenosis is not typically associated with congenitally corrected TGA: D.

CC-TGA usually comes with a VSD, pulmonary (subpulmonary) stenosis, an Ebstein-like malformation of the left-sided tricuspid valve, and complete heart block, which appears at a rate of about 2 percent a year.
Supravalvar aortic stenosis belongs to Williams syndrome, not to corrected transposition.
